chunks.heading: Tier 1: Strong Indian Community + Good Commute (Recommended)
chunks.text:
### Tier 1: Strong Indian Community + Good Commute (Recommended)

**1. Mississauga (Port Credit, Meadowvale, Downtown)**
- Distance from Toronto: 30 km west
- Commute: 30-45 min (GO Transit or car)
- Indian Community: Very strong (largest outside South Asia)
- Safety: High
- Rental 2BR: $1,800–$2,200/month
- Rental 3BR: $2,600–$3,100/month
- Job Market: 5,000+ data analyst jobs
- Best for: Balance of community, safety, commute, opportunity

**2. Markham (Downtown, Unionville, North Markham)**
- Distance: 35 km northeast
- Commute: 35-50 min
- Indian Community: Very strong (tech hub, many Indian professionals)
- Safety: Very high (upscale suburbs)
- Rental 2BR: $2,000–$2,400/month
- Rental 3BR: $2,800–$3,300/month
- Best for: Safest, most upscale, tech-friendly, excellent schools

**3. Brampton (Downtown, North Brampton)**
- Distance: 35 km west
- Commute: 35-50 min
- Indian Community: Extremely strong (Largest Indian population in Canada outside Toronto)
- Safety: Mixed (stick to Downtown/North Brampton only)
- Rental 2BR: $1,600–$1,900/month
- Best for: Budget-conscious, strong community preference

**4. Richmond Hill (North York, Bayview)**
- Distance: 32 km northeast
- Commute: 35-45 min
- Indian Community: Strong (integrated with Chinese/Korean)
- Safety: Very high
- Rental 2BR: $1,900–$2,300/month
- Best for: Quiet, safe, good schools

**EI (Employment Insurance)**
- Coverage: Unemployment, sickness, caregiving
- Eligibility: After job loss or qualifying event
- How to claim: Apply immediately after last day of work

- Coverage: Retirement (age 60/65/70), disability, survivor benefits
- Contributions: Mandatory payroll deduction
- Anil's situation: Contributions being made since 2023 in Canada

**QPIP (Quebec Parental Insurance)**
- Coverage: Maternity, paternity, adoption benefits
- Eligibility: When child arrives (2028 target)

chunks.heading: Attention Reset Plan
chunks.text: ## Attention Reset Plan

chunks.heading: Things to Avoid
chunks.text:
### Things to Avoid
- Saying "don't lose focus," "not think X," or "must concentrate"
- Fighting or blocking thoughts forcefully
- Self-judgment like "I'm broken" or "why can't I"
- Gritting teeth to hold breath focus in meditation
- Multitasking
- Long unmetered meetings
- Speaking without notes or prep
- Screens 1 hour before bed
- Irregular sleep times
- Sleeping less than 6 hours or more than 9 hours
- High-sugar meals, processed carbs, skipping breakfast, heavy meals before work, alcohol, more than 2 cups caffeine
- Rumination, all-nighters, catastrophizing about future
- Talking to yourself when alone
- Isolating when restless
- Impulse spending and no budget tracking
- Waiting to fix things "tomorrow"
- Comparing yourself to perfectly focused people
- Starting too many habits at once
- Going 7 days without practice

chunks.heading: Things to Do
chunks.text:
### Things to Do
- Say "thought appeared, back to X" neutrally
- Label intrusions as "just noise"
- Accept drift without judgment
- Use open-monitoring meditation
- Use body scan meditation
- Use walking meditation
- Limit meditation to 10-15 minutes per day
- Work single-task only
- Use 25-minute focus blocks
- Write key points before speaking
- Repeat back what others say
- Use notes during meetings
- Break tasks into micro-steps
- Schedule hard tasks at 9-11 AM
- Keep fixed sleep schedule (7-8 hours nightly)
- Use no screens 1 hour before bed
- Get morning sunlight
- Eat protein + fiber breakfast
- Keep meals low sugar
- Eat smaller meals more often if needed
- Drink 2-3L water daily
- Take omega-3 daily if appropriate
- Keep caffeine to 1 cup in morning
- Do 5 minutes breathing when restless
- Write worries down and close them
- Walk 20 minutes daily
- Track progress weekly
- Sit quietly when alone instead of self-talking
- Talk to 1 person daily
- Do 10 minutes of hobby daily
- Keep gratitude journal
- Track expenses daily
- Set auto-pay bills
- Do weekly money review
- Use 24-hour wait for spending over $100
- Write 1-year vision
- Set 3 tiny goals per week
- Review progress every Sunday
- Start with 1 habit only
- Add 1 new habit per week
- Practice at same time daily
- Aim for 90% consistency, not perfection
- Use soft focus, not gripping attention
- Keep micro-sessions short
- Use external anchors (notes, timers, lists)
- Do 30 minutes cardio 4x/week
- Do strength training 2x/week
- Have 1 social event per week
- Ask clarifying questions
- Get ADHD evaluation if needed
- Consider CBT
- Consider medication if clinically appropriate

## Decision Clarity Rules
- Separate "thinking time" from "decision time"
- Thinking time: 48 hours max to gather information
- Decision time: after 48 hours, decide — no more info gathering
- Write down criteria first
- Before any major decision, list 3 non-negotiables
- Once criteria are set, options that don't fit are automatic no
- Practice on small decisions
- Decide on coffee in 30 seconds
- Pick what to wear the same day every week
- Choose where to eat before I'm hungry
- Accept "good enough"
- At 70% clarity, have enough data
- Remaining 30% learned by doing

chunks.heading: Resume Optimization

chunks.heading: Key Strategies
chunks.text:
### Key Strategies
1. Put key skills in first 1/3 of resume (recruiter scans 6-10 seconds)
2. Use exact job title from posting in your resume header
3. Remove overqualification signals:
   - Don't list dates older than 10 years
   - Don't include senior titles unless applying for senior roles
   - Don't list salary expectations if above range
4. Highlight transferable skills if overqualified
5. Quantify results with numbers (impact shows in AI evaluation)
